name: PLA (Polylactic Acid)
chemical_makeup: Polylactic acid — an aliphatic polyester polymerised from lactic acid/lactide derived from fermented plant starch (corn, sugarcane); biodegradable under industrial composting conditions
summary: The default FDM material and the easiest polymer to print: no enclosure, almost no warp, excellent dimensional accuracy and the lowest emissions of the common filaments. The trade-off is heat and weather: parts soften near 55-60 °C, creep under sustained load, and embrittle in sunlight.

printing.notes: Heated bed is helpful but optional. Run part cooling at full after the first 1-2 layers. Modern CoreXY machines (Bambu, Prusa MK4) sustain 200-300 mm/s on PLA; legacy bedslingers sit at 40-150 mm/s. An enclosure is not just unnecessary but can be counterproductive — trapped heat promotes heat creep and clogs in some hotends. Hardened nozzles are only needed for abrasive filled PLA variants (wood, carbon, glow).

feeding.notes: The reference AMS/MMU material: Bambu's filament-guide material table lists unfilled PLA as AMS-compatible and multi-colour PLA is the standard use case. The exceptions are filled and effect grades — Bambu's AMS notes bar third-party PLA-CF/PLA-GF, certain silk PLA and glow-in-the-dark PLA from the AMS because they wear the PTFE feed tubes or break inside the feed path. Enclosure: Bambu's heat-creep guidance and QIDI's door-open table both say to remove the upper cover / open the front door for PLA, since a 35-45 °C chamber sits close enough to PLA's ~58 °C Tg to soften filament in the extruder and cause heat-creep clogs.

drying.dryness_validation: No popping/crackling or visible steam at the nozzle; glossy, consistent extrudate rather than matte or rough; no fine surface bubbles; minimal stringing on a retraction test
drying.notes: Prusa recommends 45 °C for 6 h, Bambu 55 °C for 8 h. Lower drying temperatures than PETG/ABS mean less risk of spool deformation.

storage.recommendations: Sealed bag or drybox with desiccant between uses; tolerates weeks of open air in a dry room but grows brittle after prolonged humid exposure

price.notes: 2025-2026 pricing for standard unfilled grades: budget $14-18, mid $18-22, premium/specialty $25-35 per kg

not_recommended: anything in a hot car or near heat (softens above ~60 °C)

properties.notes: Prusament PLA cites 1.24 g/cm³ and XY tensile ~51-59 MPa; other property tables run to 65 MPa. Tg and HDT@0.45MPa both fall in the 55-60 °C band, which is why PLA is unusable in hot environments. Max service temp is an estimate (Tg minus margin), not a datasheet figure.

compatibility.notes: PLA does not chemically weld to PETG, ABS, ASA, PC, PA or PP — that non-bonding is deliberately exploited so PLA and PETG each release cleanly as breakaway support for the other. PVA is the classic dissolvable support/interface for PLA (water-soluble, similar print temperatures); BVOH also works. PLA is not usable with ABS/ASA in either direction: their 90-110 °C bed temperatures deform PLA.

plate_recommendations.notes: Prints well on textured/satin PEI with no release agent at 45-60 °C bed. A glue stick is optional for awkward geometries only.
Backfilled from plate entry (Phase E reciprocity): The reference use case: strong direct bond, glossiest and flattest bottom surface of any PEI finish.

Backfilled from plate entry (Phase E reciprocity): Bare borosilicate can be too slick for PLA on its own; a thin PVA glue-stick film is the standard fix and also gives the glossy bottom finish glass is prized for.

Backfilled from plate entry (Phase E reciprocity): Listed compatible by Prusa. Adhesion is adequate rather than tenacious — this is a release-oriented coating, so add a brim for tall parts on small footprints instead of raising bed
Backfilled from plate entry (Phase E reciprocity): Vendors state no release agent needed; releases on cooling without a spatula.
Backfilled from plate entry (Phase E reciprocity): Direct print with no aid; small or thin-walled parts benefit from a brim since satin's peak grip is below smooth PEI's.

Backfilled from plate entry (Phase E reciprocity): The plate's entire reason to exist. Full adhesion at bed temperatures well below what PEI needs, which cuts warp on large flat parts and keeps the chamber cool. Parts normally pop

Backfilled from plate entry (Phase E reciprocity): The plate's whole purpose. Best PLA adhesion in the Bambu plate lineup, and Anycubic runs PLA at ~45 C here versus 60 C on a textured plate. Glue stick is applied to protect the su
Backfilled from plate entry (Phase E reciprocity): No release agent needed; parts audibly pop free once the plate cools.

Backfilled from plate entry (Phase E reciprocity): The surface's core competency. Direct print, no adhesive, reliable first layers even on a marginal bed. Filled PLAs — carbon, metal, wood, brick — are explicitly covered by the sam
Backfilled from plate entry (Phase E reciprocity): The intended use case. Natural, translucent and semi-transparent PLA show the holographic effect most strongly on the bottom face.

emissions.notes: Lowest-emission common filament. Azimi et al. (2016) measured median UFP emission around 10⁸ particles/min — roughly 100-1000x lower than ABS. The sweet odour is lactide. A normally ventilated room is sufficient for occasional printing; move air for continuous printing in an occupied space.

safety_notes: Filled and additive-heavy variants (glow, metal-filled, wood, carbon) change both the abrasion and emission picture and need a hardened nozzle — see the relevant variation entries.
additional_notes: Biodegradable only under industrial composting conditions, not in a home compost heap or landfill.

provenance.conflicts: Density: Prusament states 1.24 g/cm³, other tables cite up to 1.25 — 1.24 used. Tensile strength: Prusament XY 51-59 MPa, comparison tables up to 65 MPa, partmfg.com an outlier at 72 MPa — the 72 MPa figure is rejected and 45-65 MPa recorded as consensus. Max continuous service temperature (~50-55 °C) is inferred from Tg, not measured in any cited datasheet.
